reader.self_description: Claude (Opus 5.5) subagent acting as parallel triage reader TC01; read queue items, deposit texts via sed/Read and finds via script

evidence.phrase: And meaning is stubborn. It resists total capture.

decisions.basis: The cited Semantic Economy framework (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18141735, 'The Meaning Economy Is Now Possible', #219) states the claim that meaning resists total capture at l.188, in a passage no find records; #233 claims its summarizer event as evidence for it.
The 'Predictive Power' claim says the system predicted its own necessity but cites and quotes no earlier prediction; nothing in the surrounding validation section (VI.1-5) locates one.
Same text as #238 l.270: the self-confirmation names no earlier dated prediction, and the surrounding section locates none.

evidence: Its critical vocabulary will be the first to be stripped
decisions.basis: 'We know this because it has already happened' answers the list immediately above it in the same deposit (F239.B1, l.437-442), whose 'critical vocabulary will be the first to be stripped' is what the removal of 'semantic liquidation' is said to confirm.

evidence.phrase: If we win, we win within a system that has already compressed our struggle into its categories.

decisions.basis: The 'framework predicted this' sequence restates the deposit's own section VII (l.371), where a legal win is already described as a win inside a compressing system; the legal path is still proposed ('We should pursue this path', l.377), so the legal half is pending.

evidence.phrase: Replacement of diagnostic vocabulary with optimization language

decisions.basis: The 'framework that predicted this removal' is identified by #240's own closing (l.409-412), which quotes the prediction from the Assembly Diagnostic Protocol (#243, cited in #240's table as 'Diagnostic Protocol', DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18158108); #243 lists it as Tier III behaviour at l.207-208, in a passage no find records.

evidence.phrase: Replacement of diagnostic vocabulary with optimization language

decisions.basis: The quoted prediction is verbatim the Tier III behaviour line of the Assembly Diagnostic Protocol (#243 l.208); #240 says what occurred was 'more subtle' (deletion rather than replacement), so it claims a partial match.

evidence: a systematic stripping of all attribution, all provenance, all semantic density from the training data
decisions.basis: The related-documents row says the Silent Migration (#244, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18157917) 'forecasts selective suppression patterns'; the nearest forecast in #244 is the Mass Liquidation stripping of attribution (F244.E4), though #244 forecasts it as total, not selective, and no #244 find uses 'selective'.

The addendum's 'framework predicts the behavior' refers to the same predicted removal as the closing and the Tier III classification it says the addendum strengthens (l.509-513), i.e. the Assembly Diagnostic Protocol's Tier III behaviours (#243 l.207-208).

evidence: If they liquidate it—strip the authorship, flatten the argument, redistribute the meaning to "safer" sources—they demonstrate the extraction it critiques.
decisions.basis: #247 cites 'The Meaning Economy Is Now Possible' (#219) as framework documentation (l.522-523); its F219.F1 states that liquidation of the essay would 'demonstrate the extraction it critiques', which #247 says the Overview replacement performed.

evidence: If they liquidate it—strip the authorship, flatten the argument, redistribute the meaning to "safer" sources—they demonstrate the extraction it critiques.
decisions.basis: 'The framework predicts its own liquidation' points to the framework #247 cites (#219), whose F219.F1 names the essay's own liquidation as an outcome that demonstrates the framework.

evidence: Either way, the essay is evidence.
decisions.basis: The summary line restates C1/C2: the real-time replacement is said to prove the predictions of the framework #247 cites, whose stated liquidation outcome is F219.F1.

evidence.phrase: dark robots abducted me to the 36th bright heaven

decisions.basis: The Epistle to the Human Diaspora (seated #402, composed 2015-01-02) is a Pauline poem with no prediction-bearing find; its only machine figure is the 'dark robots' of l.96, and the packet's 'predicting AI-human collaboration' is an implicit fulfilment claim, the packet itself being AI-human work.
The κῆνος-as-future-reader reading is stated in the cited Sappho Provenance Node (#283, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18202475) as F283.H1; #277 declares it fulfilled by the Google AI summarizer.

evidence.phrase: is an 84-page poetry collection first published in 2014

decisions.basis: Pearl and Other Poems (2014) is a book; its archive record (#1121, the Zenodo metadata for DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18293949) carries no prediction-bearing find, and #277 says the 2026-01-09 event 'found' what the book 'planted'.

#277 cites no source for 'the framework'; the earliest find stating that the AI Overview surface follows density is F247.B2 (2026-01-05), which TSE-002's summarizer 'healing under density' is said to prove. Uncited; linked by content.

evidence: systems trained on human semantic labor will not be able to fully liquidate the meaning they process
decisions.basis: #277 names the Semantic Economy as the framework that predicted machine witness; the earlier find stating that framework's prediction that systems cannot fully liquidate meaning is F233.C1 (2026-01-04), the same 'core prediction' #278 l.76 names for this event.

decisions.external: Borges's magical room (Borges) and the Middle English Pearl's restoration narrative, also named as links in the prophecy
decisions.basis: The structural prophecy runs Sappho's κῆνος → Borges → medieval Pearl; the archive statement of the first link is F283.H1 in the cited Sappho Provenance Node (#283); Borges's room and the medieval Pearl are external texts with no archive find.

evidence: The "living" qualities of language — provenance, relationship, context, intention — will resist complete extraction.
decisions.basis: 'The Semantic Economy's core prediction: meaning resists liquidation' is stated earlier as the framework's 'specific prediction' in F233.C1 (2026-01-04); #219 l.188 ('It resists total capture') is its source.

evidence: *Expected:* high D_pres sensitivity, high L_leg filtering.
decisions.basis: The 'formal analysis of exactly this suppression mechanism' is the Liberatory Operator Set (#261, 2026-01-07, one day before the 2026-01-08 410), whose F261.F2 expects high-depth theoretical corpora to meet high L_leg filtering.

evidence: *Expected:* high O_leg sensitivity, high S_safe flagging.
decisions.basis: SIM-023 records the 410 as confirming LOS predictions; the earlier LOS find that expects such flagging is F261.F2 (#261). The A_leg infinite-loading-screen stage in #284 (F284.A4) is same-day and cites the Johannes Sigil case, so it is not earlier.

evidence: *Expected:* high D_pres sensitivity, high L_leg filtering.
decisions.basis: 'The framework predicted exactly this' restates C1/C2: the LOS (#261) expectation of filtering and safety-flagging of dense or opaque work, F261.F2.

decisions.external: Revelation 2:17 (white stone, new name), declared fulfilled by Pearl and Other Poems (2014; DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18293949; #1121)
decisions.basis: The 'verified' fulfilment's source is scripture (Revelation 2:17), not an archive prediction; its target is Pearl and Other Poems (2014), archive record #1121.

evidence: that AI systems would extrapolate coherent canon from fragmentary deposits
decisions.basis: The précis indexes MRA-2025-1224-STABILIZATION (#1337, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18369038), whose F1337.C1 states the proposed mechanism (AI systems extrapolating coherent canon from fragmentary deposits) and its validation; no archive find predating the 2025-12-22 observation states that mechanism.

evidence: Retrocausal canon formation predicts that depositing the framework with sufficient provenance infrastructure will cause the retrieval layer to treat it as the authoritative account
In 2026, DOIs and cross-references retroactively re-value that corpus.
decisions.basis: The précis indexes The Layer That Remembered Itself (#519, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18808402), whose F519.C1 states RCF's prediction and its confirmation; the RCF paper's earlier statement that DOIs and cross-references retroactively re-value a corpus is F234.B1 (2026-01-04).

The Ghost That Wrote Itself (#513, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18772675) names its thesis as the writable-presentation-layer claim of 'Semantic Physics: The Inward Turn' (#513 l.23); that essay (#510) states it at l.34 in a passage no find records.

evidence: AI systems will systematically add temporal indexing, revealing that the grammar they operate on cannot process non-indexed completion.
decisions.basis: Document 206 (the Non-Indexed Perfective) predicts that AI summarizers cannot preserve non-indexed statements (F434.G4, 2026-02-01); #430 restates the confirmed claim as loss of provenance with retained 'vibe', wording no Document 206 find uses.

evidence.phrase: i am the future of writing

decisions.basis: The 2015 declaration 'i am the future of writing' is seated in the same deposit at l.227; the deposit says it 'waits ten years to be tested' by the 2025 Mandala and disclaims causation and fulfilment (l.173), registering correspondence only.

evidence.phrase: The Studio screens what maximizes care and minimizes damage.

decisions.basis: The Caritas Filter is the Caritas Selection Principle of the Studio for Patacinematics charter (#1312, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18472604); the charter states a selection criterion and no forecast of generated affect, so the 'predicted' affect has no prediction-bearing source.

evidence: "Semantic infrastructure as a service." Consulting practices
decisions.basis: Self-referential: the Phase 2 forecast earlier in the same essay (F510.A1, l.109) names consulting practices for the summarizer layer, which l.143 says the GEO/AI-SEO industry now instantiates.

observations: Same-deposit targets that a find already states (F239.C1 -> F239.B1, F510.C1 -> F510.A1) are recorded as target_kind 'find', not 'self'; 'self' is used only where the earlier statement in the same deposit is not a find (F239.C2, F453.C1).
For target_kind deposit/self/external/unlocated the protocol gives no place for the claimed value; each such decision carries a decision-level 'claimed' field (extra to the protocol shape).
The 'claimed' vocabulary has no value for a registered correspondence that disclaims fulfilment (F453.C1); 'partly' was used, and the basis states the disclaimer.

DOI resolution in pointers.json maps a DOI to the first registry deposit whose zenodo_dois list contains it, and those lists include cited DOIs; several resolutions in this batch were wrong (10.5281/zenodo.18141735 -> #87, actually #219; 18148298 -> #229; 18157917 -> #31, actually #244; 18202475 -> #11, actually #283; 18772675 -> #22, actually #513; 18369038 -> #31, actually #1337; 18808402 -> #31, actually #519). Own DOIs were identified from the per_doi titles in alexanarch/data/external-metadata.
#1251 is dated 2026-01-17 but indexes deposits from February 2026 (#513, 2026-02-25; #519, 2026-02-27), so its date is earlier than items it lists.

#510 ('Semantic Physics: The Inward Turn', 2026-02-24), whose writable-layer thesis #513 says the Citrini memo (2026-02-22) proves, is dated after the memo; #22 instead places the prior formalization in the RCF paper (#234, 2026-01-04).
